- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4) and price is rising, model often overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overcorrects — cap forecast rise to 2–3% per day to avoid lagged overreaction.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.5) and price is trending up, model often underestimates — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast.  
- If last 3–5 days show mean reversion (price oscillating around 75–80), model tends to ignore it — adjust forecast to align with recent 10-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 2–5% in early cycles — apply +2% offset to initial forecast if sentiment is bullish.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a dip, model often delays reaction — forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
